title: Go-to-market Battlecard Suite and Sales Enablement Play
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Objective: Produce a comprehensive, modular enablement package for Sales and Customer Success to support the runtime-1.20 launch. The package should make it fast for reps to understand positioning, key technical tradeoffs, customer objections, and demo flows so they can run discovery and close deals within a single call.

Deliverables (minimum):
- Executive one-pager battlecard (2-sided PDF): positioning, top 6 use cases, target customer profile, pricing/commit guidance, competitive differentiators, objection handling.
- Detailed FAQ (living doc): answer set for common product, deployment, security, and pricing questions; links to Confluence, release notes, and support KB.
- Talk tracks (framed by persona): 3x 2-minute scripts (technical buyer, product buyer, procurement) plus cross-sell prompts.
- Demo scripts and walkthroughs: 2 canonical demos (quick 10-min feature demo, deep 25-min technical demo) with step-by-step prompts, expected outputs, and troubleshooting checklist.
- Enablement slide deck (editable): customer stories, SLOs, performance benchmarks, cost/levers, and rollout timeline.
- Rehearsal plan: schedule for sales ops and CS bootcamps, with metrics for readiness (roleplays completed, QA pass rate).

Scope notes: This ticket focuses on content creation, coordination, and first-pass reviews. Production of final collateral assets (design polish, video recordings) will be tracked as follow-ups. Where technical detail is required, work with ENG-4810 (runtime perf) for validated benchmarks and DOC-214 for canonical copy. Design assets to be delivered by DES-1117 for finalization.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Battlecard PDF completed and approved by Sales Lead and PM; 2) FAQ contains answers for top 12 anticipated Qs, linked to supporting docs; 3) Demo scripts execute end-to-end in internal dry-run with no critical blockers; 4) Rehearsal scheduled with Sales Ops and CS with >= 80% attendance target; 5) Assets uploaded to Drive + Confluence and referenced in release notes coordination doc.
